title: Sort by Any Key Path
hints: A key path like `\Person.age` can read a property from any value.
In an extension on `Sequence`, sort using `$0[keyPath: keyPath] < $1[keyPath: keyPath]`, generic over a `Comparable` value type.
`func sorted<V: Comparable>(by keyPath: KeyPath<Element, V>) -> [Element] { sorted { $0[keyPath: keyPath] < $1[keyPath: keyPath] } }`.
jsBridge: Key paths like `\Person.age` are typed property references, a type-safe version of passing `'age'` strings to lodash's `sortBy(people, 'age')`. The compiler knows `\.age` is `KeyPath<Person, Int>`, so a typo is a compile error.

compass.q: `_.sortBy(arr, 'agee')` fails silently at runtime. What does `sorted(by: \.agee)` do?
Key paths vs closures `{ $0.age }`: where can a key path go that a closure can't (Hashable, SwiftData `#Predicate`, `@dynamicMemberLookup`)?
SwiftUI `ForEach(items, id: \.id)` and `Table` columns use key paths. Why a key path rather than a closure there?
